To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dust in the spiral galaxy M81 has a peak emission wavelength of ∼160 μm, and that this peak is consistent with dust being heated to a maximum of ∼30 K.
the 160 and 250 μm emission is primarily due to warm dust in the disc and bulge heated by evolved stars, whereas the 70 and 500 μ m emission is due to a mix of dust heated by evolved and young stars.
the 70 μ m emission from M81 is dominated by dust heated by the AGN and young stars, while the 160– 500 μ m emission traces 15 – 30 K dust heated mainly by evolved stars.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dust emission from M81.
understanding the nature of dust in galaxies.
understanding the dust emission in M81 and the implications for understanding the heating mechanisms of dust in galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M81 is an active star forming galaxy.
the 160-500 μm dust emission traces the bulk of the dust in the galaxy whereas the 70-160 μm emission traces the dust in the star forming regions.
the 70 μμ emission is a mixture of dust heated by evolved and young stars, whereas the 160–300 μm emission is dominated by dust heated by evolved stellar populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 70 μ m emission in M81 is dominated by dust emission heated by the active nucleus and young stars while the 160– 500 μm emission is dominated by dust heated by evolved stellar sources.
the 70–160 μm emission is primarily dominated by dust heated by evolved stellar populations and that the 160 μm–1 mm emission is dominated by dust heated primarily by evolved stars.
the 160 and 250 μm emission is dominated by the evolved stellar population while the 70 and 350 μm emission is more dominated by star formation activity in the galaxy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ratio of wave bands in the far infrared can be used as a tracer of the relative importance of dust heated by evolved and young stars in nearby galaxies.
the 160 μm band is the best Herschel band for studying dust emission from the diffuse interstellar medium in nearby galaxies.
